page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.48xlarge is an ARM64-based general-purpose server powered by 192 dedicated physical cores of the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processor. Operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz, each core features 64 KB L1d cache and 2 MB L2 cache, backed by a 96 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It includes 11400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps, running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 382376.39 and a PassMark CPU score of 107019.88. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, reaching 729.18 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations and 327.45 GB/sec for large-block write operations. Database and caching capabilities are demonstrated by a PassMark database operations score of 61965.11 and Redis SET performance of 506.95 million operations per second.

Despite strong multi-core capabilities, single-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2009.1. The hardware lacks x86-specific vector and matrix extensions such as AVX-512 and AMX. LLM inference benchmarks show a distinct tradeoff: while prompt processing for a medium 7B model is top-tier at 388.37 tokens/sec, text generation for a small 135M model is poor at 13.22 tokens/sec. This profile makes the server highly effective for multi-threaded workloads, large-scale database operations, high-throughput web serving, and data compression tasks, rather than single-threaded execution or real-time LLM text generation.
description: Amazon Web Services m9gd.48xlarge is an ARM64 general-purpose server featuring 192 dedicated physical cores of the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processor running at 2.8 GHz. It is configured with 768.0 GB of RAM, 11400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth under the Nitro hypervisor. Benchmarks show top-tier multi-core CPU performance, high memory bandwidth, and strong database execution, including 506.95 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core performance is average, and the architecture lacks AVX or AMX instruction sets. LLM text generation speeds are also limited, with a small model generating only 13.22 tokens per second. This server is optimized for highly concurrent workloads, high-throughput web serving, and database applications requiring substantial local storage.
